answer: Low-conductance cut detection resists sybils: a sybil region, however large internally, connects to the honest core across only a thin set of attack bridge edges, so the cut separating it has low conductance. A random walk from the honest oasis mixes rapidly inside the real graph but stalls crossing the narrow bridge into the fake cluster, so walks rarely land there and the region's trust mirror stays near zero. The bottleneck an attacker cannot widen without forging many reciprocated honest edges caps total sybil trust by the cut size, not the fake count.
